speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Lyme Disease (Borrelia burgdorferi) causing septic arthritis of the wrist and cutaneous manifestations (erythema migrans or acrodermatitis chronica atrophicans).

The normal CBC, ESR, CRP, and WBC differential, combined with the history of a self-resolving knee pain (likely a previous monoarticular Lyme arthritis episode), recent camping in Minnesota (endemic area), and sexually active status (potential co-infection or unrelated STI), strongly suggest a delayed or disseminated tick-borne illness. The absence of systemic inflammatory markers points away from typical bacterial septic arthritis. Please confirm if the skin lesions are migratory (expanding rash) and if you have a history of tick bites.
